question: A sum of ₹625 is invested in a bank at 16% interest per annum compounded annually. On maturity, the amount payable becomes ₹841. Find the time period of the investment.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for 1 year at 16% = 1 + 16/100 = 116/100 = 29/25

Ratio of final Amount to Principal = 841 / 625

We can observe that 841 / 625 = (29 / 25)²

Since the ratio is exactly the square of the 1-year multiplying factor, the time required is 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹625

Amount (A) = ₹841

Rate of Interest (R) = 16% per annum compounded annually

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
• 
 
 Principal (P)
 ₹625
 
 Amount (A)
 ₹841
 

 

 Rate (R) = 16%
 Time = n years
 A = P × (1 + 16/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ 841 = 625(1 + 16/100)ⁿ

⇒ 841 / 625 = (1 + 4/25)ⁿ

⇒ 841 / 625 = (29/25)ⁿ

⇒ (29/25)² = (29/25)ⁿ

⇒ n = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n.

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate can be directly calculated as: R + R + (R × R)/100 = 2R + R²/100.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years is given by the formula: D = P(R/100)².
